newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN STATISTICS SERVICE BRAVES BUDGET CUTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN STATISTICS SERVICE BRAVES BUDGET CUTS.

text.p: Budget cuts had forced the Central Statistical Service to pay greater attention to rationalising its surveys and conducting business more on a user-pays basis, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday.

Speaking during the debate on the CSS's 1997/98 budget, which has been cut by and effective 14 percent (excluding the cost of last year's census) to 84.9 million rand, Manuel said that some surveys could justifiably be abandoned as obsolete.
"Some can be retained on a user-pays basis...but others remain of national strategic importance," Manuel said, adding that a need for new surveys was emerging.
As a result, strategic plans had been drawn up to be considered under the planned new multi-year budgeting system "so that it may render the statistical service which the new South Africa demands".
The CSS already expected to handle three household surveys worth seven million rand on a user-pays basis this year covering subsistence agriculture, child labour and the victims of crime.
"The user-pays principle will also shortly be applied regarding economic series which are of specific rather than general interest, which would otherwise have to be abandoned," Manuel said.

The CSS would start using data gathered by other government departments to improve the Business Register while reshaping its labour-related surveys so that they could be of better use to the labour and trade and industry departments.
CSS staff were helpin other departments improve their data collection and preparing materials that could help the general public become more familiar with how to use statistics in everyday life.

"In these ways, improved statistical information will contribute to more efficient and cost-effective operations not only within departments but among them, and not only within government but in its service to civil society," Manuel said.
The CSS used to fall under the office of Deputy President Thabo Mbeki but was recently transferred to Manuel's ministry.
